title: Minds: how a non-player decides, and why it is built this way
summary: Design rationale and implementation plan for the non-player decision subsystem: per-actor viewsheds, a phased perceive stage, typed game choices, minds without combat, and goal-keyed flow fields.
notes: Subsystem design doc under docs/design/ (the repo's 'how one subsystem works, and why' folder), classified DOC for consistency with sibling fields.md. Signals compete: it records explicit owner decisions ('Decision, Nate, 2026-09-16': actors carry their own Viewshed; Health is two fields current and max) and a declined alternative (Brain<A, C> type parameter), which are ADR-like, and it states firm type and schedule contracts (DecideSet order Sense, Notice, Offer, Perceive, Minds, Game; PerceiveSet phases Begin, Roster, Filter, Annotate; Decision::Own(Box<dyn Choice>); FlowFields keyed by goals, profile, opens_doors, away), which are SPEC-like. It has no ADR Status or Decision/Consequences sections, covers many decisions rather than one, and has no formal schema tables, so it was not promoted; the synthesizer may want to treat the two named Nate decisions as locked and the set and type contracts as technical constraints. Doc says it was built 2026-09-16, so section 3 describes current state and sections 2 and 4 are history. Guide chapters 4 and 9 and the tutorial are mentioned by name without paths. Output filename uses a path-derived suffix instead of the SHA-256 hash because no shell was available to compute it, matching the sibling convention.
